newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends down but off lows, in range.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends down but off lows, in range.

text.p: CSCE world sugar drifted to a lower close Wednesday amid thin, featureless trade, floor sources said.
Trade buying out of the Far East lifted prices to the highs early but speculative selling and local liquidation pressured prices to the lows.
Some light short-covering near the close boosted contracts off their lows but prices remained stuck in a 20-point trading range between 10.95 and 10.75 basis May.

"The market will slide lower until we reach a technical area that would trigger a bigger selloff," Refco analyst Anne Prendergast said. "And logically, it would seem the surplus of supply should begin to affect the market."

Brazilian sugar output, meantime, is seen unchanged at 13 million tonnes in the 1997/98 crop year, equal to production in the current marketing season, the head of the Industry and Commerce Ministry's primary commodity department, said today.
Prendergast pegged support at 10.50 cents in May, adding that a move below 10.47 cents, the overhead target prior to the recent rally, would trigger stops.
On the upside, market sources see resistance at Monday's high of 11.08 cents and then at 11.19 cents, the high made February 20.
CSCE May sugar closed 0.02 cent lower at 10.86 cents a pound, having ranged from 10.95 to 10.76 cents a lb. The deferred contracts were 0.09 to 0.04 cent weaker.
Volume was estimated at 15,569 lots compared with the official 10,321 lots Tuesday.
Dockworkers at Brazil's Paranagua port launched a strike today, halting all activity involving general cargo including orange juice, wood and cotton. The strike had no effect on sugar.
